events.body: Does this only reproduce on OpenBSD?

> Does this only reproduce on OpenBSD?

I haven't yet observed this issue on any [other platforms](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly).

Looks like the connection to one of the addresses (60.0.0.1) is just getting stuck for no apparent reason and never completes the handshake. I don't have an explanation, but as a wild guess:  maybe related to 34bed0ed8c which introduced a workaround only for FreeBSD?

> Looks like the connection to one of the addresses (60.0.0.1) is just getting stuck for no apparent reason and never completes the handshake. I don't have an explanation, but as a wild guess: maybe related to [34bed0e](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/34bed0ed8c449a3834927cec3447dbe6c74edf3d) which introduced a workaround only for FreeBSD?

Thanks! Done in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36145.

Unfortunately, that doesn't help: https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/actions/runs/33663232206/job/100358725821.

> Looks like the connection to one of the addresses (60.0.0.1) is just getting stuck for no apparent reason and never completes the handshake.

The following [patch](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin/commit/d3db3e7997a62199798e5971a49698a4e2deb817) helps to get rid of such stuck connections:
```diff
--- a/test/functional/p2p_private_broadcast_retry_v1.py
+++ b/test/functional/p2p_private_broadcast_retry_v1.py
@@ -143,6 +143,7 @@ class P2PPrivateBroadcastRetryV1(BitcoinTestFramework):
                 f"-onion={self.tor_proxy.conf.addr[0]}:{self.tor_proxy.conf.addr[1]}",
                 "-test=addrman",
                 "-v2transport=0",
+                f"-peertimeout={int(10 * self.options.timeout_factor)}",
             ],
         ]
 
```

But that is just hiding the symptom, not fixing the underlying cause?
